candidates.exact_span: industrial user was on a schedule to attain compliance with effluent limits, indicate the date the schedule was issued and the date compliance is to be attained
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether an industrial user is on a compliance schedule, and the schedule dates, can change which effluent limits are enforceable during Federal FY2025 and whether related reporting obligations apply for that period.

candidates.exact_span: A list of all significant industrial users whose authorization to discharge was terminated or revoked during the preceding 12 month period and the reason for termination
candidates.computation_change_reason: Termination or revocation of discharge authorization during the lookback period can change whether monitoring and reporting were required for those users in FY2025 and how missing or absent results should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: A report on any interference, pass through, upset or POTW permit violations known or suspected to be caused by industrial contributors and actions taken by the permittee in response
candidates.computation_change_reason: Documented interference, pass through, upset, or related violations can establish alternative evidence states for periods lacking ordinary numeric results, affecting how missing or anomalous monitoring evidence is interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: The results of all influent and effluent analyses performed pursuant to Part II(A)(1)(c) above
candidates.computation_change_reason: The scope of Part II(A)(1)(c) analyses determines which monitoring was required, which reported measurements exist for limit comparison, and whether absent results reflect a documented no-data state versus inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The monthly average water quality based effluent concentration necessary to meet the state water quality standards as developed in the approved technically based local limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of these technically based local limit concentrations determines which enforceable numeric discharge limits apply for monthly-average compliance comparisons versus report-only values.

candidates.exact_span: Any new introduction of pollutants into the treatment works from an indirect discharger which would be subject to Sections 301 and 306 of the Act if it were directly discharging those pollutants
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a new pollutant introduction occurred, and how that phrase is interpreted, can trigger additional notice and monitoring obligations in FY2025 and affect whether missing results reflect conditional non-requirement or unresolved evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Any substantial change in the volume or character of pollutants being introduced into the treatment works by a source introducing pollutants into the treatment works at the time of issuance of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a change in pollutant volume or character qualifies as substantial can change applicable monitoring and notice requirements during FY2025 and how periods without results should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: Adequate notice shall include information on (i) the quality and quantity of effluent to be introduced into the treatment works, and (ii) any anticipated impact of the change on the quality or quantity of effluent to be discharged from the POTW.
candidates.computation_change_reason: What constitutes adequate notice, and whether required quality, quantity, and impact information was provided, can affect whether conditional monitoring obligations were triggered and whether related evidence gaps are documented or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: All effluent monitoring conducted in accordance with Part (II) (A) (1) (c) above shall meet the Minimum Quantification Levels (MQLs) shown in MQL's at Appendix A of Part II below.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the MQL requirement and the referenced Appendix A values can determine whether effluent monitoring satisfied permit obligations and whether reported or missing results constitute adequate evidence for compliance evaluation.
